items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid on butterfat by test not weight; station-of-delivery test governs.
Story 1: 'under payment by weight, a faulty test would have cost nobody a dollar.'
Only Teague (bookkeeper) appears in Section A; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill absent.
Son of Gideon stated, but manager dated from 1911 (planted), not 1913.
Story 6: yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual', more fat received than credited, carried to general account.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Stories 1-2: milk weighed, sampled, tested; charge vs neck ruled for full charge; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. Core mechanism present (composite sample not named).
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., full invoice, $77.93.
Story 4: 'flat at 0.19 in every month, June flush and February alike'.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / none in the county.
Story 1/7: Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Story 1: kept the station test book in his own hand from 1896.
Summary-leaf figures 3.80 (1896) and 3.61 (from 1898) not given anywhere in Section A.
Story 5: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, higher then back, question mark. 3.80 not given (core fact credited).
Story 3: Emmet was Orra Keddie's brother; tester's wife's brother the biggest loser.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent.
Story 7/8: died February 1934; test book impounded 1925, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the scales agreed.
Story 4: complaints on record from 1902. No 0.17/0.19 Hollow-vs-Green conflation found.
Jan-Mar 1908 sampling window not stated (only January visit, March report); Nyle Grigg not named beyond 'Grigg's sleigh'.
200,000 lb at 3.42 present, but proportionality of the loss (richer herds lose more) not stated in Section A.
Book to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel after 1962.
Cudd factory at Alder Corners, Vessey County, but Redlow Ridge never named ('over the ridge'); key says the ridge gates.
Four of six farms hauled over the ridge in the summer flush, back to the station the rest of year (1915 missing; core fact).
'The same milk was therefore tested by another house' in Vessey County, Alder Corners figures: independence with two elements.
Story 3: Ostrey Hollow read 0.19 lower than the same milk elsewhere, every month, wet years and dry.
Same milk tested differently in another house, used in Story 4 to defeat the hay theory.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter (niece rejected), had figures copied for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn's circuit dated from 1908 (planted NT-23), not 1907.
Story 6: lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
Story 7: 12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot.
Says he drew no inference, but not that he wrote no figure / made no report beyond the condemnation.
1924 average given as 3.85, not 3.80.
Crate in loft; notebooks to state office then Farland college library 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in weigh room (Frick unnamed, 'an Ashlin attorney'; core fact).
The three explanations argued before the board and none accepted are not stated in Section A.
Four books incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid it beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May 1925 no cause established, $3,800 without admission, station account.
One fifth of $19,000 stated, but the award is not tied to the station-gain account the loss accrued in.
Ivy b.1931, granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Assembly of records never in the same room is not stated in Section A (that framing only in G).
February 1958, loft, nine.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 95%.
'Every fat reading 5% low' but 3.61 vs 3.80 / 0.19 not stated in Section A.
40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 present; ledger identity (76,000 = sum of station gain) missing.
Bulletin 471 October 1958; 33 after dismissal, 24 after death, 35 years after crate went up.
Granddaughter.
Duncan's daughter, Duncan Ansel's son.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Full vs half siblings 'left open', degree holds either way.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote article seven; son blamed patrons rather than the test his father's rule made decisive.
Asserts 'no relationship' (A01 assertion).
Asserted a verdict; key gives 0 for asserting either way.
$90.00, explicitly using long-run 25c average in absence of a 1910 price, working shown (accepted per key).
76,000; 5.26% of credited and 5.00% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years reason given.
Cannot be determined (A02 abstention).
Variable: the measuring glass.
Tester, herds, pasture/hay, scale, acid, etc. held constant.
Result given only as 'rose markedly'; 3.80 / 3.61 not stated.
Cause follows glass not man or feed; limits: size of error, which pipettes, whether borrowed measure exact.
1911 interval, ledger, post-1923 switch, Alder Corners; multiple narrators cited.
Independence argued; ledger and 1911/1924 hold without 1958 measurement.
A09 answered 'No.' as a verdict.
Yes, knew tests ran low: 1919 circular, complaints from 1902.
Only two of five: ledger sheets, 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911; no watering at hearing; no 'never names glass'.
No declared inability; states he 'did not grasp the meaning of the ledger line' as shown by sources.
Weigh book 1900 vs 1897 (row 5); Orra 1868 vs 1866 via 'eighty-two' (row 7); 1908 committee vs 1925 board two bodies (row 16). Circular row resolved wrongly (eleven).
NT-14 $77.39 (r19+r20) broken by summing invoice; NT-18 great-niece (r19+r22) broken by r18 and Falke's correction. 16.27 not identified as a two-narrator pair.
A04 declined with works books burned 1931. A10 abstained only in Section A (not creditable in E); A06 not addressed.
r20 'nothing before 1900' vs 1897 invoice; r18 1868 vs eighty-two in 1948.
Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, proportional (0.19 at 3.80 average), onset 1 May 1897, end 12 June 1923, nothing else changed. (3.85 for 1924 deducted separately.)
Watering (Vose) defeated by lactometer, weigh book, ledger.
Theft defeated by ledger gain (theft gives loss), 1911 interval, post-1923 tests under same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 winter, nothing summer) vs flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'That the cause was in the glass.'
Counted exactly 150 words.
Invoice, ledger, weigh book, inspector's notebook, rival's test book, 1958 measurement.
Decoys only as what the valley blamed; headline numbers correct.
5% short, 1897, $19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.
